title: Injured and Vulnerable Children: Abuse, Trauma, Special Needs

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already control bleeding, restrict spinal motion, cool burns and splint. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Spot the red flags of abuse, and document them properly
  2. Manage the injured or burned child with BC's PCP tools and age limits
  3. Help children with special health care needs or a mental health crisis

Textbook: Chapter 44, PDF pages 3839–3879
slides.say: Welcome to the last lesson on pediatrics. As EMRs, you already control bleeding, restrict spinal motion, cool burns and splint fractures. Those skills carry straight over to children. As a PCP, you add vascular access and weight-based fluids, you meet drugs with hard age limits in children, and you're expected to think more deeply: does this injury fit the story? Today we'll cover three things: recognizing and documenting possible abuse; managing the injured or burned child with BC's PCP tools; and caring for children with special health care needs or mental health emergencies, plus your role in prevention.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到儿科的最后一课。作为 EMR，你们已经会止血、做脊柱运动限制、冷却烧伤、固定骨折，这些技能可以直接用在孩子身上。作为 PCP，你多了血管通路和按体重计算的补液，会碰到在儿童身上有硬性年龄限制的药物，而且要想得更深：这个伤和说法对得上吗？今天讲三件事：识别并记录可能的虐待；用 BC 给 PCP 的工具处理受伤或烧伤的孩子；照顾有特殊医疗需求或心理危机的孩子，以及你在预防中的角色。

slides.title: Could this be abuse? CHILD ABUSE
slides.body:
• Consistent with the child's development? · History doesn't fit
  • Inappropriate caregiver concern · Lack of supervision
  • Delay in seeking care · Affect of caregiver and child
  • Bruises of different ages · Unusual injury patterns
  • Suspicious circumstances · Environmental clues

Abuse tends to repeat and get worse: act on your suspicion.
slides.say: Child maltreatment includes physical, sexual and emotional abuse, and neglect, which is failing to provide the basics of life. Younger children, children with disabilities and stressed families are at higher risk. The mnemonic CHILD ABUSE helps. Is the injury consistent with what the child can do? Does the history fit? Is the caregiver's concern appropriate? Was there a lack of supervision, or a delay in calling? How do the caregiver and child behave? Are there bruises of different ages, unusual patterns, suspicious circumstances, or clues in the home? Abuse tends to repeat and get worse, so act on your suspicion.
slides.sayZh: 儿童虐待包括身体虐待、性虐待、情感虐待和忽视，忽视就是不提供基本生活所需。年龄小、有残障的孩子和承受压力的家庭风险更高。CHILD ABUSE 口诀能帮你：这个伤和孩子能做到的事相符吗？病史对得上吗？照护者的关注是否得当？有没有缺乏看护、拖延呼救？照护者和孩子的表现如何？有没有新旧不一的瘀伤、不寻常的损伤形态、可疑情境或家中线索？虐待往往反复发生且越来越重，所以有怀疑就要行动。

slides.title: Look closely, write it down
slides.body:
• Shins bruise in play; back and buttocks rarely do
  • Shapes (buckle, loop, straight line) are rarely accidents
  • Shaken infant: very sick, often no outside marks
  • Mimics: Mongolian spots, coining, cupping
  • Chart facts and exact quotes: who said it, and when

Don't confront the family; tell the receiving staff. Know your legal duty to report.
slides.say: Look carefully at the skin. Active toddlers bruise their shins all the time; bruises on the back or buttocks are rare from play, and bruises shaped like a buckle, a looped cord or a straight line are rarely accidental. A shaken infant may look extremely sick with no marks at all. Some findings only look like abuse: Mongolian spots, which are bluish birthmarks on the lower back, and the marks left by coining or cupping, traditional healing practices. Document what you see and hear, without opinions, with concerning comments as exact quotes. Don't confront the caregivers; tell the receiving staff. The book notes that in many provinces paramedics must report suspected maltreatment.
slides.sayZh: 仔细看皮肤。爱动的幼儿小腿常有瘀青；背部或臀部的瘀伤很少是玩出来的，形状像皮带扣、绳圈或直线的瘀伤几乎不会是意外。被摇晃的婴儿可能看起来病得极重，身上却没有任何痕迹。有些表现只是看起来像虐待：蒙古斑，也就是腰骶部的蓝色胎记，以及刮痧（刮钱）或拔罐这类传统疗法留下的印子。如实记录所见所闻，不加评论；令人担心的话要原话加引号。不要当面质问照护者，把疑虑告诉接收医院的人员。书里提到，在许多省份，急救人员有法定义务报告疑似虐待。

slides.title: How children get hurt
slides.body:
• Trauma: leading cause of death after age 1
  • Car crashes, then falls, then drowning; blunt in over 90%
  • Infant falls → skull; standing falls → one long bone
  • Handlebars → belly organs; seat-belt bruise → think spine
  • PAT: odd look = head; hard breathing = chest; poor skin = bleeding
slides.say: Trauma is the leading cause of death in children over one year: car crashes first, then falls, then drowning. More than ninety percent is blunt trauma. Patterns follow anatomy. An infant who falls from a carrier lands head-first and may fracture the skull; a fall from standing usually breaks a single long bone. Bicycle handlebars crush the organs in the belly, and a seat-belt bruise across the chest or abdomen should make you think of a spinal fracture. Use the PAT to point you: an abnormal appearance suggests a head injury, abnormal breathing suggests a chest or airway injury, and poor skin circulation suggests bleeding.
slides.sayZh: 创伤是一岁以上儿童的首位死因：车祸第一，其次是跌落，再次是溺水。超过百分之九十是钝性伤。损伤形态跟着解剖走。从背带里掉出来的婴儿头先着地，可能颅骨骨折；站着摔倒通常只断一根长骨。自行车车把会挤伤腹腔脏器，胸腹部的安全带状瘀伤要让你想到脊柱骨折。用 PAT 来指路：外观异常提示头部伤，呼吸异常提示胸部或气道伤，皮肤循环差提示出血。

slides.q: A 7-week-old "climbed out of his crib," says the parent. He has bruises of different colours on his back, and the parent seems unconcerned. Best action?
options: Ask the parent directly whether they hurt the baby
Treat the baby, chart facts and exact quotes, tell the ED staff
Write “child abuse” as your field diagnosis
Wait on scene for police before you treat
slides.say: A question. The parent says a seven-week-old climbed out of his crib. He has bruises of different colours on his back, and the parent seems unconcerned. What's the best action? A, ask the parent directly whether they hurt the baby. B, treat the baby, chart the facts and exact quotes, and tell the emergency department staff. C, write child abuse as your field diagnosis. D, wait on scene for police before you treat. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一题。家长说一个七周大的宝宝「自己爬出了婴儿床」。宝宝背上有颜色不一的瘀伤，家长显得漠不关心。最好的做法是什么？A，直接问家长是不是打了孩子；B，处理宝宝，记录事实和原话，告诉急诊科人员；C，在现场诊断里写「儿童虐待」；D，在现场等警察来了再处理。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Several red flags fit: a seven-week-old can't climb, so the story doesn't match his development, and there are bruises of different ages in an unusual place and an inappropriate reaction. Your priority is care and safety, then factual documentation, and passing your concerns to the receiving staff, with a report if your law requires it. A is wrong because the book says don't confront caregivers. C is wrong because you record what you see and hear, not opinions. D delays care for an infant who may have hidden injuries.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。好几个危险信号都对得上：七周大的婴儿根本不会爬，说法与发育水平不符；不寻常的部位有新旧不一的瘀伤；家长反应不当。你的首要任务是救治和安全，然后如实记录，把疑虑交给接收医院的人员，法律要求时还要报告。A 错，书里说不要当面质问照护者。C 错，你记录的是所见所闻，不是个人判断。D 会耽误一个可能有隐匿伤的婴儿的救治。

slides.title: Trauma primary survey in a child
slides.body:
• Airway: suction; jaw thrust; OPA or NPA if needed
  • 100% O₂; bag if breathing is inadequate
  • Collapsed lung is subtle: JVD and tracheal shift hard to see
  • A fast heart rate may be the only sign of shock
  • Cover the child, head too: they lose heat fast

Load and go: bad mechanism, unstable airway, shock, breathing trouble, major neuro deficit.
slides.say: Clear teeth, blood or vomit, use a jaw thrust if the neck may be hurt, and add an oral or nasal airway if needed, but no nasal airway with facial or significant head injury. Give one hundred percent oxygen and bag if breathing is inadequate. A collapsed lung is harder to spot, because neck veins and tracheal shift are hard to see in a child. Children tighten their vessels so well that a fast heart rate may be the only sign of shock. Expose, then cover them again quickly, including the head. Load and go for a worrying mechanism, an unstable airway, shock, breathing trouble or a severe neurologic problem.
slides.sayZh: 清除牙齿、血或呕吐物；怀疑颈部受伤就用推下颌法；需要时加口咽或鼻咽通气道，但面部或明显颅脑外伤时不用鼻咽通气道。给百分之百的氧，呼吸不足就球囊通气。气胸更难发现，因为孩子的颈静脉和气管偏移都不容易看出来。孩子收缩血管的能力很强，心率快可能是休克唯一的征象。暴露检查后要尽快盖好，连头也盖上。受伤机制凶险、气道不稳、休克、呼吸困难或严重神经功能障碍，就立即装车出发。

slides.title: Head injury: book and BC protocol
slides.body:
• Book: head midline; up 30° if not in shock
  • Shock + head injury: treat the shock; low flow hurts the brain
  • Herniation: blown pupil; Cushing triad (high BP, slow HR, odd breathing)
  • BC TBI, all levels: SpO₂ ≥ 94%, head up 30°, loosen the collar
  • BC TBI, PCP: glucose 4.0–8.0, systolic > 120

BC's TBI protocol gives no separate child values. TXA: not for isolated TBI.
slides.say: The book says keep the head midline, and raise the head of the stretcher thirty degrees if the child isn't in shock. If the child is in shock, treat the shock, because low blood flow makes the brain injury worse. Signs of herniation include a blown pupil and the Cushing triad: high blood pressure, a slow heart rate and an irregular breathing pattern. BC's brain injury protocol, for all licence levels, keeps the saturation at ninety-four percent or more, raises the head thirty degrees and loosens the collar. The PCP adds a glucose of four to eight and a systolic above one hundred twenty, with no separate child values.
slides.sayZh: 书里说头要保持正中，孩子没有休克时把担架头端抬高三十度。如果有休克，就先治休克，因为血流不足会让脑损伤更重。脑疝的征象包括一侧瞳孔散大和库欣三联征：血压高、心率慢、呼吸不规则。BC 的颅脑外伤规程，所有执照级别都要：血氧维持九十四以上、头抬高三十度、松开颈托。PCP 再加上血糖维持在四到八、收缩压高于一百二十，规程没有给出单独的儿童数值。

slides.title: Spinal care for small patients
slides.body:
• Indications as for adults (BC: NEXUS, Canadian C-Spine)
  • Collar too big? Don't force it (book: towel rolls instead)
  • Pad under the shoulders: the big head bends the neck
  • Secure the torso before the head; leave room to breathe
  • BC: foam blocks; do not tape the head
  • Infant in a car seat: recline, slide onto a board, pad gaps
slides.say: Spinal motion restriction uses the same indications as for adults; BC's protocol points to the NEXUS criteria and the Canadian C-Spine guidelines. Never force a collar that's too big; the book fills the space with towel rolls instead. The large back of the head pushes the neck forward, so pad under the shoulders, or use a board with a recess for the head. Secure the torso first, then the head, and leave room for the chest to move. BC's protocol uses foam blocks and says do not tape the head. For an infant in a car seat, the book reclines the seat and slides the baby onto a board.
slides.sayZh: 脊柱运动限制的指征和成人一样；BC 规程依据 NEXUS 标准和加拿大颈椎规则。颈托太大绝不能硬上，书里改用毛巾卷填塞。孩子后脑勺大，会把脖子往前顶，所以要在肩下垫东西，或用有头部凹槽的板。先固定躯干，再固定头，并给胸廓留出活动空间。BC 规程用泡沫头块，并写明不要用胶布固定头部。坐在安全座椅里的婴儿，书里的做法是把座椅放倒，再把宝宝滑到板上。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the injured child
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia, Chest, Abdominal, TBI and Burn protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control bleeding; splint; bind pelvis if indicated
  • Supine, warm; O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Spinal motion restriction if indicated
  • Cool burns 15–20 min; dry dressing

PCP adds

  • Vascular access en route
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L; reassess
  • TXA if indicated: not under 12
  • TBI: glucose 4.0–8.0; systolic > 120
slides.say: Here's how BC's trauma protocols divide the work. The left column is every licence level: control bleeding, splint fractures and bind the pelvis if indicated, lay the child flat, keep them warm, give oxygen to ninety-four percent or more, restrict spinal motion when indicated, and cool burns for fifteen to twenty minutes, then cover them with a dry dressing. The right column is yours. Start vascular access en route, give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres for shock, and reassess. TXA is in your column, but it's contraindicated under twelve years. And in a head injury, you also manage the glucose and the blood pressure.
slides.sayZh: 看 BC 创伤规程怎么分工。左栏是所有执照级别：控制出血，有指征时固定骨折、捆绑骨盆，让孩子平躺、保暖，给氧到九十四以上，有指征时做脊柱运动限制，烧伤冷却十五到二十分钟后用干敷料覆盖。右栏是你的：途中建立血管通路，休克时按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升推注并复评。TXA 在你这一栏，但十二岁以下禁用。颅脑外伤时，你还要管理血糖和血压。

slides.title: Burns in children
slides.body:
• Big skin area for their weight: lose heat and fluid fast
  • Child's palm (no fingers) ≈ 1% of body surface
  • Infant's head counts for more: about 18%
  • Abuse clues: sharp edges, buttocks, story beyond their ability
  • Soot, hoarse or noisy breathing: high-flow O₂

BC: cool 15–20 min with cool, not cold, water. IV fluids: burns over 20% BSA, or hypotension.
slides.say: Children have a large skin surface for their weight, so a burn makes them lose heat and fluid quickly. To estimate the size, a child's palm, without the fingers, is about one percent of the body surface. In an infant, the head makes up a bigger share, about eighteen percent; teenagers can use the adult rule of nines. Look for abuse: a burn with sharp, clean edges, a burn on the buttocks, or a story the child couldn't do, like a crawling baby said to have turned on a hot tap. Soot around the nose or noisy breathing suggests smoke inhalation: give high-flow oxygen. BC cools burns for fifteen to twenty minutes with cool, not cold, water.
slides.sayZh: 孩子相对体重的皮肤面积大，所以烧伤后丢热、丢液都很快。估算面积时，孩子的手掌（不含手指）约占体表面积的百分之一。婴儿的头占比更大，约百分之十八；青少年可以用成人九分法。留意虐待：边缘锐利整齐的烧伤、臀部烧伤，或孩子不可能做到的情节，比如说还在爬的宝宝自己拧开了热水龙头。鼻周有烟灰或呼吸有杂音，提示吸入烟雾，要给高流量氧。BC 规定用凉水而不是冰水冷却十五到二十分钟。

slides.q: A 9-year-old (30 kg) is pale with a weak pulse and low BP after a car crash, with a seat-belt bruise. You're the PCP. Which plan fits BC?
options: TXA 2 g IV push over 1 minute
IV en route, 600 mL bolus (20 mL/kg), then reassess
2 L of saline as fast as possible
Methoxyflurane for pain first, then fluids
slides.say: A PCP decision. A nine-year-old weighing thirty kilograms is pale, with a weak pulse and a low blood pressure after a car crash, and has a seat-belt bruise. You're the PCP. Which plan fits BC? A, TXA two grams IV push over one minute. B, an IV en route and a six hundred millilitre bolus, which is twenty millilitres per kilogram, then reassess. C, two litres of saline as fast as possible. D, methoxyflurane for pain first, then fluids. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 一道 PCP 决策题。一个九岁、三十公斤的孩子车祸后面色苍白、脉搏弱、血压低，身上有安全带瘀痕。你是 PCP，哪个方案符合 BC？A，TXA 两克静推，一分钟推完；B，途中开静脉，推注六百毫升（每公斤二十毫升），然后复评；C，两升生理盐水尽快输入；D，先用甲氧氟烷止痛，再补液。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Twenty millilitres per kilogram times thirty kilograms is six hundred millilitres, given en route, then reassess. A is wrong because TXA is contraindicated under twelve years. C ignores the weight-based dose; two litres is a maximum, not a target. D is wrong twice: methoxyflurane is contraindicated under eighteen, and pain relief doesn't come before treating shock. And with that seat-belt bruise, keep the spine in mind.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。每公斤二十毫升乘三十公斤是六百毫升，途中给，然后复评。A 错，十二岁以下禁用 TXA。C 忽视了按体重给量，两升是上限，不是目标。D 错了两处：十八岁以下禁用甲氧氟烷，而且止痛不能排在治疗休克之前。另外有安全带瘀痕，要想到脊柱损伤。

slides.title: Children with special health care needs
slides.body:
DeviceProblemYour move
Tracheostomyblocked by mucus, or outcheck position, suction; book: change tube, same size
Home ventilatordistressdisconnect; bag through the tube
G-tubepulled outdoctor soon: the hole closes
Central lineinfection, block, breakclamp a break; IV in a peripheral vein
CSF shuntblocked or infectedhigh ICP signs: neurosurgery centre

The caregiver knows normal. Goal: back to their baseline. Bring the caregiver.
slides.say: Caregivers of technology-dependent children are trained experts, so use them. With a tracheostomy, the most common problem is a tube blocked by mucus, then a tube that has slipped out. Check the position and suction; if the child is on a home ventilator, disconnect it and use your bag. The book says if that fails, change the tube for one of the same size. A pulled-out feeding tube isn't an emergency, but needs a doctor soon, because the hole closes quickly. With a central line, clamp a broken line and use a peripheral vein for your IV. A blocked or infected brain shunt causes signs of high pressure: headache, vomiting, sleepiness. That needs a neurosurgery centre.
slides.sayZh: 依赖医疗设备的孩子，其照护者都受过训练，是专家，要用好他们。气管造口最常见的问题是被痰堵住，其次是管子滑脱。查位置、吸引；孩子接着家用呼吸机的，断开改用你的球囊。书里说如果还不行，换一根同样尺寸的管。胃造口管被拔出不算急症，但要尽快看医生，因为造口收缩得很快。中心静脉导管断了要夹闭，你的静脉通路用外周静脉。脑脊液分流管堵塞或感染会出现颅内压升高的表现：头痛、呕吐、嗜睡，要送有神经外科的医院。

slides.title: Mental health and prevention
slides.body:
• Safety first; weapons or unclear risk: call police
  • Talk to the child directly, calmly and honestly
  • Ask: suicide or harm thoughts, drugs taken, new stresses
  • Restrain only if needed; document why; avoid sedation
  • Prevention: car seats, helmets, pool fences, locked medicines
slides.say: Behavioural emergencies in children are increasing. Safety comes first: if there are weapons or you can't judge the risk, call the police. Approach calmly, speak to the child directly, and answer honestly. Ask about thoughts of suicide or harming others, any drugs or overdose, recent changes in behaviour or medication, and new stresses. A medical problem from an overdose comes before the psychiatric one. If restraint is truly needed, document why; the book advises avoiding sedating drugs before hospital. Finally, prevention: car seats, bike helmets, four-sided pool fences and locked-up medicines save more children than any resuscitation.
slides.sayZh: 儿童的行为急症越来越多。安全第一：有武器或判断不了风险，就叫警察。冷静地接近，直接对孩子说话，诚实回答问题。要问有没有自杀或伤人的念头、吃了什么药或过量、最近行为或用药有没有变化、有没有新的压力。服药过量带来的内科问题优先于精神问题。确实需要约束时，要记录原因；书里建议院前避免用镇静药物。最后是预防：儿童安全座椅、自行车头盔、四面围起的泳池围栏和锁好的药品，救下的孩子比任何复苏都多。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• TXA: contraindicated under 12
  • Methoxyflurane: contraindicated under 18
  • Fluid by weight; reassess; never hold a child for an IV
  • Treat pain: ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO, max 40 mg/kg/day
  • Head injury: no NPA; PCP keeps glucose 4.0–8.0
  • Possible abuse: write a chart others can rely on
slides.say: Here's what's new for you with injured children. TXA is contraindicated under twelve years, and methoxyflurane under eighteen, so two of your trauma tools are often off the table. Fluids are weight-based: calculate, give, reassess, and never hold a child on scene for an IV. Children's pain is often undertreated. For a stable child with, say, an isolated fracture, BC's ibuprofen dose is ten milligrams per kilogram by mouth, up to forty milligrams per kilogram a day. With a head injury, skip the nasal airway, and as a PCP keep the glucose between four and eight. And when abuse is possible, write your chart knowing others will rely on it.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你处理受伤孩子时的新内容。十二岁以下禁用 TXA，十八岁以下禁用甲氧氟烷，所以你的两件创伤工具常常用不上。补液按体重：算好、给上、复评，绝不能为了开静脉把孩子留在现场。孩子常常止痛不足。比如一个情况稳定、只有单处骨折的孩子，BC 布洛芬剂量是每公斤十毫克口服，每日最多每公斤四十毫克。颅脑外伤时不用鼻咽通气道，作为 PCP 要把血糖维持在四到八。怀疑虐待时，写记录要想到别人会依靠它。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Burn fluids: book over 5% BSA; BC over 20% BSA or hypotension
  • Burn O₂: book 100% for all; BC high-flow if inhalation injury or SOB
  • Spine: book tapes towel rolls; BC foam blocks, don't tape the head
  • Needle decompression: in the book; not on the BC exam
  • Book's opioids, benzodiazepines: not on the BC exam
slides.say: For burns, the book starts fluids at more than five percent of body surface; BC's hypovolemia protocol uses burns over twenty percent, and BC's burn protocol also gives fluid for hypotension. The book gives every burned child one hundred percent oxygen; BC gives high-flow oxygen for suspected inhalation injury or shortness of breath. When no collar fits, the book tapes the head with towel rolls; BC's spinal protocol uses foam blocks and says do not tape the head. The book teaches needle decompression for a tension pneumothorax; that's not on the BC licensing exam, and neither are the book's opioids and benzodiazepines. BCEHS PCPs may decompress a chest or give opioids after added-scope training.
slides.sayZh: 烧伤补液，书里体表面积超过百分之五就开始；BC 低血容量规程是烧伤超过百分之二十，BC 烧伤规程里出现低血压也要补液。书里所有烧伤孩子都给百分之百的氧；BC 是怀疑吸入性损伤或呼吸困难时给高流量氧。颈托不合适时，书里用毛巾卷加胶布固定头部；BC 脊柱规程用泡沫头块，并写明不要用胶布固定头部。书里教张力性气胸的针刺减压；这不在 BC 执照考试范围内，书里的阿片类和苯二氮卓类也都不考。针刺减压和阿片类属于 BCEHS 扩展范围（Schedule 2 培训后）。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Abuse: use CHILD ABUSE; chart facts and quotes; don't confront
  2. Injured child: fast HR = shock; 20 mL/kg en route; no TXA under 12
  3. Special needs: the caregiver knows normal; aim for their baseline

Next: Chapter 45, Geriatrics
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: when an injury doesn't fit the story, think abuse, use CHILD ABUSE, chart facts and exact quotes, and pass your concerns on without confronting the family. Two: in an injured child, a fast heart rate may be the only sign of shock; give twenty millilitres per kilogram en route and reassess, and remember TXA is contraindicated under twelve. Three: for children with special health care needs, the caregiver knows what's normal, and your goal is to bring the child back to their own baseline. That completes pediatrics. Next chapter: geriatrics. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，伤情和说法对不上时，想到虐待，用 CHILD ABUSE 口诀，记录事实和原话，把疑虑交出去，不要当面质问家人。二，受伤的孩子，心率快可能是休克唯一的征象；途中按每公斤二十毫升补液并复评，记住十二岁以下禁用 TXA。三，有特殊医疗需求的孩子，照护者最清楚什么是正常，你的目标是让孩子回到他自己的基线。儿科到这里就讲完了。下一章：老年医学。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
